answer: A stake-gated identity bond resists Sybil floods: each new agent locks a bond sized like carving a tunnel through karst rock, released only after sustained peer-attested work. Cheap throwaway clones cannot fund many bonds at once, while honest orchard-scale fleets amortize the lock across real output. Bond size tracks network load the way a glacier advances slowly—raising cost as attack volume grows—so the attacker pays compounding capital and opportunity cost instead of free identities.
